english.title: Treaty firm fail to give the appropriate UK regulator seven days notice of carrying on of a regulated activity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a Treaty firm which qualified for authorisation under Schedule 4 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 but was not carrying on in the United Kingdom the regulated activity or any of the regulated activities which it had permission to carry on there, failed at least seven days before it began to carry on such a regulated activity, to give the appropriate UK regulator, namely the

(A)_[Financial Conduct]_
(B)_[Prudential Regulation]_

Authority, written notice of its intention to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 6(1) and (4) of Schedule 4 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

english.notes:
(i) Paragraph 6(2) of Schedule 4 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that a 'Treaty firm' means a person:-
(a) whose head office is situated in an EEA state (its "home state") other than the United Kingdom and (b) which is recognised under the law of that State as its national.
(ii) In proceedings against a person for an offence under paragraph 6 of Schedule 4 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, it is a defence for the defendant to show that he / she took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.
(iii) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the Authority or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(iv) In relation to this offence, the appropriate UK regulator means -
(a) where any of the activities to which the notice relates is a PRA-regulated activity, the PRA;
(b) in any other case, the FCA

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
